note: #2767 item 13 (a CRLF body's captured Setext candidate-text line keeps its trailing "\r", defeating the thematic-break exclusion and misreading two ordinary "---" lines as a Setext heading): the comment's own specific mechanism (a false-positive misread of two ordinary thematic breaks) does not reproduce -- under CRLF, NEXT_HEADING_PATTERN's search returns no match at all for every construction tried (the underline line's own trailing "\r" blocks the pattern's own line-end alternative), a total false-negative miss rather than a false match (PARTIAL). The consequence is still real and dangerous in the same family: with the boundary never found, the Acceptance Criteria section scan becomes unbounded and silently absorbs a later, unrelated section's substantive bullet, turning a should-fail placeholder-only AC section into a wrongly-passing one purely because of CRLF line endings -- this entry's own verifiability: pass verdict (below) is exactly that wrongly-passing outcome; an otherwise-identical LF body fails verifiability instead, confirming the delta. Notably, the sibling pattern in triage-structural-evidence.mts (NEXT_ATX_HEADING_PATTERN) already carries an explicit "\r?\n" fix for exactly this class of bug; suitability-triage.mts's own NEXT_HEADING_PATTERN does not. Unrelated to item 13's own claim: checkAutonomy (Check 6) also fails on this body, because its own literal "- TBD" placeholder line independently matches the UNRESOLVED_CHOICE_SOURCE pattern -- an artifact of the placeholder text choice, not a #2767 gap.
